fixes.explanation: Law is a good guess, but it's not the word here. The verse calls the staff in their hands "My wrath." (Isaiah 10:5) The LORD is speaking about His anger, not handing down rules. I think the word "staff" had your mind drifting toward shepherds.

Not this time, baker. Isaiah 10:6 says God dispatches Assyria against a people destined for His rage "…to take spoils and seize plunder…" So the statement is true, and the verse says it right out loud. I know, I know, I went looking for a trick too. Sometimes the verse just hands you the answer, and I still get suspicious.

Good guess, but the text doesn't say that. Assyria asks, "Is not Samaria like Damascus?" in a string of questions that pair cities together (Isaiah 10:9). The way he lines them up, his point is that they're alike, not that one is tougher. I think he's saying one more city on the list is no big deal.

Right. He pairs cities up: "Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?" (Isaiah 10:9) The point is that they're alike, not that one is tougher to take. I think he's bragging that none of them is any different from the next.

That's the one. Assyria says his hand seized "…the idolatrous kingdoms whose images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria…" (Isaiah 10:10) Images are idols, and he says theirs surpassed the ones in those two cities. So his brag is about taking kingdoms whose idols surpassed these.

Twigs would be fair for a nest, but that's not what he says. The line is, "Like one gathering abandoned eggs, I gathered all the earth." (Isaiah 10:14) So it's eggs he's gathering. I think he's pretty pleased with himself about it.

Not this time, baker. The passage asks, "Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it?" (Isaiah 10:15) The question after it, about a saw, points the same way, and so do the rod and the staff. Nobody expects an axe to say it's the boss, so the expected answer is no.

Shelter is a gentle word, but it's not the one here. The verse says, "And the Light of Israel will become a fire, and its Holy One a flame." (Isaiah 10:17) Fire and flame are the words the verse uses. So the answer is fire.

Nice picture, baker, but the verse doesn't say that. It says, "The remaining trees of its forests will be so few that a child could count them." (Isaiah 10:19) Hills aren't mentioned. A child counting them would be done before I finished tying my apron, and I'm slow with that knot.
